speakers.speaker: daniel-steinberg
speakers.bio: Daniel loves to write about, teach and code for Apple platforms using Swift. Daniel is the author of more than a dozen books including the best-selling books A Functional Programming Kickstart, A SwiftUI Kickstart, A Swift Kickstart and Dear Elena. Daniel presents iOS, Functional Programming, SwiftUI, and Swift training and consults through his company Dim Sum Thinking.

speakers.speaker: peter-friese
speakers.role: Staff Developer Advocate on the Firebase team at Google
speakers.bio:
Peter is a Staff Developer Advocate on the Firebase team at Google, helping developers build amazing experiences and high quality apps using Firebase and AI.

With a passion for empowering developers and fostering innovation, Peter works tirelessly with the Firebase team to make his vision of “cutting short the time to magic” a reality.

Peter is also the author of the book Asynchronous Programming with SwiftUI and Combine: Functional Programming to Build UIs on Apple Platforms and host of the YouTube show Firebase After Hours, in which he and his colleagues explore Firebase in a light-hearted and fun setting.

He has written code in BASIC, C, ObjectPascal, Java, Kotlin, Xtext, JavaScript, TypeScript, Objective-C, and a number of home-grown DSLs - but his all-time favourite is Swift.

You can follow Peter on Twitter, Mastodon, Threads, and YouTube.

speakers.speaker: dharam-kapila
speakers.bio:
Dharam is an iOS developer based in Denmark. He’s the creator of “Funnel: Quick Capture”, an indie app he’s been building since 2023. Today he works as a senior software engineer at Obsidian.

You can follow Dharam on X.

speakers.speaker: raluca-bujor
speakers.role: iOS Chapter Lead at Deutsche Bank
speakers.bio:
Raluca is an iOS Chapter Lead at Deutsche Bank with 8 years of experience in iOS development. She is passionate about SwiftUI, modern mobile architecture, and building scalable, user-friendly applications.

Beyond engineering, she enjoys organizing iOS community meetups, mentoring developers, and sharing knowledge with fellow mobile engineers. Outside of tech, she loves fitness, staying active, and bringing the same consistency and discipline from sports into everyday work.

speakers.speaker: emanuele-agosta
speakers.role: UX and learning design at Tesla
speakers.bio: Emanuele is a product designer and Apple Certified Trainer. He was a senior design mentor at the Apple Developer Academy in Naples from 2019 to 2025, designing curriculum and mentoring 300+ international developers a year in UX/UI, product design, spatial computing, and accessibility. He now works on UX and learning design at Tesla in Amsterdam.

speakers.speaker: matvei-novoselov
speakers.role: iOS and visionOS Software Engineer at Sony Group
speakers.bio: I am an iOS and visionOS Software Engineer working in London, UK at Sony Group. Apple Developer Academy Alumni. Apple Swift Student Challenge 2025 winner. Co-author of a scientific research paper on visionOS and Spatial Computing at the ICSR International Conference on Social Robotics published by Springer. Co-author of Virtual Film Maker Patent SYP361478US01.

speakers.speaker: alex-antonov
speakers.bio: Experienced iOS developer based in The Netherlands, worked in different fields and ended in healthcare startup. Every Apple event drinks apple cider and eats apple cakes. Easily distracted by cows.

speakers.speaker: cyril-cermak
speakers.bio: Hi I am Cyril, an iOS System Architect with over a decade of experience building cutting-edge mobile applications. I am specializing in leading teams to deliver state-of-the-art mobile engineering solutions. My professional passions include software engineering, iOS security, modular architecture, and reverse engineering iOS apps. I frequently share my expertise through workshops and talks, aiming to inspire others and drive innovation and a practical security mindset within the mobile development community.

speakers.speaker: douglas-hill
speakers.bio: Douglas spent many years as the iOS team lead at Nutrient (previously known as PSPDFKit) and recently switched to work across a wider range of technologies at the company. He’s a long-time organiser of the NSLondon iOS developer community.

speakers.speaker: caitlin-steele
speakers.bio: Caitlin Steele has worked as a developer and led design on tools developers use every day, including Trello, Confluence, and Jira. She’s a Certified OOUX Strategist and has keynoted SwiftCraft, with talks at Pragma and iOSKonf. She works on the human side of building software at Thoughtful Apes.

speakers.speaker: mihaela-mihaljevic
speakers.bio: Mihaela is a Swift engineer who works from first principles: to understand a framework, she rebuilds it and measures parity against the original. That habit produced SlayerMotion, a from-scratch pure-Swift reimplementation of Apple’s UI, graphics, and motion pipeline. She writes about Swift internals at aleahim.com.

speakers.speaker: ekaterina-volkova
speakers.bio: Ekaterina Volkova is a Software Engineer at Zalando, where she builds products used by millions of customers. She has spoken at international conferences including Swift Heroes, NS Spain, and SwiftLeeds. Her talks combine real engineering experience with the human side of software development, exploring how developers grow, adapt and thrive in an industry that never stops changing.

speakers.speaker: jeroen-leenarts
speakers.role: Senior iOS Engineer at Dawn Technology
speakers.bio:
Jeroen is a Senior iOS Engineer at Dawn Technology and the organizer of Do iOS. He has been building software since 2002, and iOS has been his main focus since 2012.

He previously led iOS developer relations at Stream, where the job was to make a complex product feel simple for other developers. Before that he led iOS work at Achmea and consulted at Xebia. Across that path he has moved between Python, Java, Objective-C, and Swift — and between writing code and talking with the people who have to live with it.

Outside the day job he runs AppForce1, a podcast and writing practice about real iOS work rather than polished demos, and he has chaired CocoaHeadsNL since 2013. He is the author of Lead Developer.

You can follow Jeroen on X and at appforce1.net.
